title: Generative AI as a lab partner: a case study
extended_summary:
This paper examines how high school students used ChatGPT during a physics laboratory session and what that reveals about the potential role of generative AI in school laboratory work. The authors were interested in how students perceived useful interactions with ChatGPT, how they actually used it while working on a lab, and whether such interactions supported problem solving and conceptual understanding.

The intervention was an intentionally designed high school physics lab on acoustic levitation and the speed of sound in air. Students were given access to the free version of ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) alongside the lab manual, textbook, formula book, and calculator. The lab instructions were deliberately somewhat vague so that students would likely need to consult ChatGPT for help with formulas, analysis, and conceptual questions. Data came from video recordings of seven student groups, chat logs, written notes, and pre/post group interviews.

The study involved 19 Swedish high school students across Physics 1, 2, and 3 courses, including both second- and third-year students. The context was a school/university-linked physics lab in Sweden, and the analysis focused on qualitative patterns in how students interacted with ChatGPT and how prior knowledge shaped their ability to judge its answers.

The authors conclude that ChatGPT can function as a kind of lab partner or quick source of information, but its usefulness depends strongly on students’ prior physics knowledge and their ability to evaluate output critically. More knowledgeable groups used ChatGPT more productively, while less knowledgeable groups were more easily misled or used it in a superficial way. The paper argues that generative AI may support lab work and problem solving, but only when students have enough subject knowledge and guidance to avoid over-trusting inaccurate or confusing responses.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI chatbot based on GPT models, used for answering questions, explaining concepts, and generating text or formulas.
identified_tools.use_case: High school physics students used the freely accessible GPT-3.5 version of ChatGPT during an acoustic levitation lab to get help with understanding the phenomenon, identifying equations for analysis, converting units, and answering discussion questions.

findings.finding_summary: In this qualitative case study (n=19 across 7 lab groups), ChatGPT was sometimes useful for providing equations, brief explanations, and quick guidance during the physics lab, especially for students with more prior knowledge who could evaluate its answers. However, it also produced vague, confusing, or incorrect guidance in some cases, and weaker-knowledge groups often accepted outputs uncritically or were misled by them.
findings.measure: Qualitative observations from lab video, chat histories, and pre/post group interviews about usefulness, trustworthiness, and problem-solving interactions

quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative/mixed-methods case study rather than an experimental design, so the evidence is best classified as yellow. The paper provides rich observational detail, but no causal estimate or controlled comparison.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported impact is mixed and context-dependent: some groups benefited from concise explanations and formula lookup, while others were confused or misled. No effect size is reported, so the overall impact is unclear rather than clearly positive or large.
